rationale: The Ukrainian domestic glide bomb may carry CRPA anti-jam antennas, the standard answer to GNSS jamming that degraded Excalibur and JDAM-ER.

rationale: Mesh radio was Russia's second adaptation to losing Starlink; self-healing networks spread to long-range drones after the cutoff, and by September relay chains controlled drones 150–175 km out.

effect: roughly doubles delivery times
rationale: Russia pulled stocks back to 50 and later 100 km; moving depots past the ~85 km range roughly doubles delivery times.

rationale: Khartiia's search-and-destroy group and the Kupiansk Tactical Group cleared the forests and villages north of Kupiansk, retook Kindrashivka and Radkivka (the pipeline exit area), reached the Oskil and cut the pipeline route and northern supply lines (21 Oct per Butusov, 12 Dec per Khartiia).

rationale: A drone spots an emergence and artillery or bomber drones saturate the hole; of about 600 Russians who tried in 100 days only eight got through, the 77th Airmobile Brigade caught about 40 near the Oskil, and Khartiia said in May 2026 that about 95% of crossers were killed or wounded within about 10 minutes of emerging.

effect: too fast to be caught
rationale: At about 500 km/h, jet Gerans are beyond current interceptor drones.

rationale: The SBU calculated the film thickness needed to hide the explosives from customs scanners; at Taman the truck was opened but not X-rayed.

rationale: A sea-skimmer at 3–10 m gave about 2 min of warning at best, and the crew reportedly failed to react.

rationale: Drones with terminal AI guidance need no live link and are unaffected by the Kupol jammer.

rationale: The Russian move to fibre-optic FPVs began to undercut EW-based protection.

effect: units struck

rationale: Pre-H-hour strikes on command posts left Russian units unable to receive orders; after the July HIMARS strikes Russia could no longer stockpile shells beside its guns.

rationale: With roads under Rubikon fibre-optic FPV attack, Kazhan bomber drones flew food, water, fuel and grenades around the clock.

rationale: Ukrainian SAM units killed up to 100 KABs in September–November 2025, the first real anti-KAB capability.

effect: would ignore GNSS jamming altogether; reported, unconfirmed
rationale: Section 2 table, Jul–Sep 2026 row.

Both sides hand the last mile to ground robots; Ukrainian UGV missions, mostly logistics, rose to 25,143 in August 2026 and the General Staff credits UGVs with up to 30% fewer casualties.
With no encryption keys and poorly trained operators, Russian traffic could be monitored by Ukraine.
Decoys costing $30–1,000 drew Russian cruise missiles and Kalibrs costing $3–6M; dummy air-defence sites soaked up munitions.
Ukrainian gun crews had to displace 2–15 minutes after opening fire under Russian precision fires designated by drones.
Rotations were run at night and in bad weather because about half of Ukrainian casualties were taken in the rear during rotation and resupply.
Russia netted roads (e.g. 2+ km between Bakhmut and Chasiv Yar, February 2025) and placed drone-detector traffic lights along supply routes.
Russia responded to middle strike with these measures, including moving military fuel in ambulances and bread vans.
Ukraine used HARM against air defence during the interdiction campaign.
Russia set radar reflectors along both Antonivskyi bridges as a counter to HIMARS interdiction (text lists them among Russian counters; no effect stated).
A fuel pipeline along the Antonivskyi rail bridge kept fuel flowing despite the strikes.
After the Oct 2022 truck bomb, bridge security moved under the FSB, checks became heavier, and fuel and ammunition were barred from the bridge.
Russia barred fuel and ammunition, imposed 3.5 t then 5 t weight limits, and moved dangerous cargo to ferries and ships; military trains fell from 42–46 a day to 4–5.
The Sergey Kotov was sunk by Ukrainian USVs while guarding the southern approaches in Mar 2024, and the Navy hit a Sobol and a Grachonok guarding the bridge on 30 Apr 2026.
A Pantsir-S1M was deployed on the bridge itself in mid-Aug 2024; Russia claimed 12 ATACMS aimed at the bridge downed on 15 Aug 2024.
Barges were positioned to be towed forward to shut the channel under the arch, the gap that a continuous barge line must leave for shipping.
From Aug 2024 hedgehogs were sunk on the seabed in 1–2 layers and metal fences put around the pillars; the barrier system was built against surface and underwater drones.
